templates.text: The tactile system is profoundly underdeveloped, with minimal response to even deep pressure.
Severe tactile hyposensitivity renders the skin nearly insensate to touch and temperature.
A profound deficit in tactile processing prevents the perception of light touch or gentle stroking.
Tactile input is severely muted, with a delayed and blunted response to physical contact.
The tactile channels are grossly deficient, failing to register most forms of cutaneous stimulation.
There is a near-complete absence of functional tactile sensation across the body surface.
Tactile perception is critically impaired, with no discernible reaction to non-noxious touch.
A severe tactile processing deficit results in an unresponsive, hypoesthetic state.
The neural pathways for tactile sensation are severely underdeveloped and non-functional.
Tactile awareness is profoundly diminished, with skin contact registering as a faint, distant signal.
A gross impairment of the tactile system leaves the infant insensible to texture and gentle pressure.
Tactile receptors are present but their central integration is severely disrupted and ineffective.
The capacity for tactile discrimination is absent due to severe peripheral and central deficits.
Tactile feedback is critically deficient, providing almost no information about contact or surface.
A profound tactile hyposensitivity mutes all sensation of light touch, deep pressure, and vibration.
The tactile sensory apparatus is severely underdeveloped, yielding a minimal and delayed response.
Tactile sensation is grossly attenuated, with responses only to intense, prolonged stimulation.
Severe underdevelopment of tactile pathways results in a near-total lack of cutaneous awareness.
Tactile input fails to generate meaningful cortical representation, leaving touch unperceived.
A critical deficit in tactile processing abolishes the perception of gentle stroking and holding.
Tactile channels are non-functional, with a response latency of over {seconds} seconds to firm touch.
The tactile system is severely compromised, unable to distinguish between smooth and rough surfaces.
Profound tactile impairment renders the infant unaware of most environmental contact and handling.
Tactile sensation is present only at a primitive, non-localized level with severe hyposensitivity.
A severe developmental lack of tactile integration prevents normal rooting and grasping reflexes.
Tactile perception is critically absent, with no observable startle to sudden light touch.
The infant exhibits profound tactile indifference due to severely underdeveloped sensory pathways.
Tactile feedback loops are grossly deficient, offering minimal proprioceptive or exteroceptive input.
A profound deficiency in tactile processing mutes the sensory experience of cradling and swaddling.
Tactile responsiveness is severely blunted, requiring pressure exceeding {grams}g to elicit a faint reaction.
